title: SCA Minhag of the Week 160: "Bar Missvah- American Birthday Customs"

summary: Mr. Mosseri discusses two new-world customs that equate a Bar Mitzvah with a birthday. He explains the custom of a rabbi presenting a gift such as a Siddur or Chumash to the boy at the end of prayers. He also discusses the 13-candle lighting ceremony on a cake created by kosher caterers in the United States.

questions: Why do some synagogues present a Siddur or Chumash to a Bar Mitzvah boy?
Did the custom of giving gifts to a Bar Mitzvah boy at prayers exist in the past?
Where did the candle-lighting ceremony on a Bar Mitzvah cake come from?
What connection is made between lighting candles on a cake and an aliyah to the Sefer Torah?
